title: Terraform global settings resources: URL lists, end user notification and browser control

prose.text: A few global settings resources have rules that the schema does not show: caps on the URL lists, a rejected content type in notifications, and special handling of empty or equivalent values in browser control. Each is a place where a plan can differ from what the API holds.

prose.label: URL lists.
prose.text: {{url-lists-capped}} The two lists are written with two separate calls: [[zia.terraform.multi-step-writes]].

prose.label: End user notifications.
prose.text: {{eun-no-javascript}} {{issue-472-javascript-and-escape-drift}} Whether the escape drift remains is open {{gap:issue-472-escape-drift-current}}.

prose.label: Browser control.
prose.text: {{profile-needs-real-value}} {{absent-profile-recorded-as-none}} {{profile-change-skipped-when-empty}} {{any-normalised-by-api}} The data-source side of the empty profile is in [[zia.terraform.data-source-fidelity]].

checks.do: Whether a browser control plan fails with NOT_SUBSCRIBED on a tenant without Cloud Browser Isolation, and whether the profile block holds a real value.
Whether a browser control list drift is the ANY, NONE and empty-list equivalence rather than a real change.
Whether a notification text containing a script tag is the cause of an HTTP 406 on the end user notification resource.
Whether the allowlist or denylist length is within the schema caps.

url-lists-capped.statement: The `zia_security_settings` schema caps the allowlist (`whitelist_urls`) at 255 entries and the denylist (`blacklist_urls`) at 275000 entries.

quotes: "whitelist_urls": { Type: schema.TypeSet, Optional: true, Computed: true, MaxItems: 255, Description: "Allowlist URLs whose contents will not be scanned. Allows up to 255 URLs.",
"blacklist_urls": { Type: schema.TypeSet, Optional: true, Computed: true, MaxItems: 275000, Description: "URLs on the denylist for your organization. Allow up to 275000 URLs.",
"zia_security_settings": resourceSecurityPolicySettings(),

eun-no-javascript.statement: The provider documents that the ZIA API does not accept JavaScript tags in end user notification text attributes and answers them with an HTTP 406 Rejected error.

quotes: The ZIA API currently does not accept JavaScript tags in notification text attributes. Using JavaScript tags will result in an HTTP 406 Rejected error.

profile-needs-real-value.statement: The browser control resource treats a `smart_isolation_profile` as configured only when its `id`, `name` or `url` is non-empty, because the service reports an all-zero profile object on tenants that have none and a bare block in HCL flattens to empty strings.

quotes: // smartIsolationProfileConfigured reports whether a smart_isolation_profile // value holds an actual profile. The presence of the block is not sufficient:
// the service reports an all-zero profile object on tenants that have none, // and a bare block in HCL flattens to empty strings.
id, _ := profile["id"].(string) name, _ := profile["name"].(string) url, _ := profile["url"].(string) if id != "" || name != "" || url != "" { return true }

profile-change-skipped-when-empty.statement: A smart isolation profile change is sent only when one side holds a real profile; the code comments that an all-empty block left in state by earlier releases is not worth sending because tenants without a Cloud Browser Isolation subscription are answered with 403 NOT_SUBSCRIBED.

quotes: // A profile change is only worth an update when one side holds a real

// profile. State written by earlier releases can contain an all-empty // block, and dropping that is not a configuration change worth sending — // tenants without a Cloud Browser Isolation subscription are answered // with 403 NOT_SUBSCRIBED.
if smartIsolationProfileConfigured(before) || smartIsolationProfileConfigured(after) {

absent-profile-recorded-as-none.statement: When the service reports no profile, Read records that absence and so clears an all-empty block left by an earlier release, except that state holding a real profile the service did not echo back is left alone to avoid false drift.

quotes: // that too — an absent profile is a real answer here, and writing it through // is what clears an all-empty block left behind by an earlier release.
The one // case to leave alone is state that holds a real profile the service did not // echo back, which would otherwise be dropped and show up as drift.

any-normalised-by-api.statement: The Browser Control API accepts the value ANY in a request but normalizes it server-side to an empty list or ["NONE"], treating ANY, NONE and no entries as equivalent; the provider keeps a declared ["ANY"] in state when the API returns that no-entries form so later plans converge.

quotes: // "ANY" in the request is accepted but normalized server-side to either an // empty list (bypass_plugins / bypass_applications) or ["NONE"]

issue-472-javascript-and-escape-drift.statement: Provider issue #472, still open, reports that `zia_end_user_notification` `custom_text` holding JavaScript was rejected, which a repository member put down to the API not supporting JavaScript tags in the payload and escalated as an internal bug, and that on provider 4.4.9/10 a heredoc using the Terraform escape `$${` produced a change back to `${`; the member answered that the provider sets the HCL as returned by the API and pointed the reporter to Zscaler support.

quotes: ## Comment (MEMBER, 2025-09-03) @(user) This is an api issue and has been escalated. The API does not support JavaScript tags in the payload.
## Comment (MEMBER, 2025-09-09) @(user) WebUI and API are not the same. An internal BUG issue has been raised with our engineering team
it wants to do a change and swap back to escape from native `${` result
the provider sets the HCL as returned by the API
- there's still a problem with 4.4.9/10 and not respecting heredoc format
the terraform escape characters `$${` to pass the java vars thru
uses the arg `custom_text`
- zia_end_user_notification
If there are problem still problems please contact Zscaler support and make reference of this GitHub Issue.

issue-472-escape-drift-current.title: Whether the current provider still rewrites `$${` in end user notification text
issue-472-escape-drift-current.blocks: saying that escaped template syntax in notification text plans cleanly
issue-472-escape-drift-current.detail: Issue 472 reports the drift on v4.4.9 and v4.4.10, was never reported fixed, and the vendored provider is much later, so whether `$${` still produces a plan change is not shown. Apply a notification whose `custom_text` holds `$${` and plan again.
